hydro_flattening_sentences_verbatim: Hydro-flattened Bare Earth DEMs represent water bodies in a cartographically and aesthetically pleasing manner, and are not intended to accurately map water surface elevations.

In a Hydro-flattened DEM, water surfaces are flat and level for lakes with a greater area than two acres, and gradated for rivers or other long impoundments (e.g., reservoirs) that are wider than 100 feet, and tidal areas.
This raster dataset provides hydro-flattened high resolution terrain elevation data in the Salt Lake County area of the Utah LiDAR project.

verbatim_quotes.claim: Seamless DEM is built from diverse sources
verbatim_quotes.quote: Seamless 3DEP data are derived from diverse source data that are processed to a common coordinate system and unit of vertical measure.
verbatim_quotes.source: USGS 1/3 Arc Second n41w113 tile metadata (FGDC XML), U.S. Geological Survey

verbatim_quotes.quote: Ground Conditions: Lidar was partially collected in fall 2016, while no snow was on the ground and rivers were at or below normal levels.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 LiDAR - Great Salt Lake AOIs, project-level FGDC metadata, Quantum Spatial, Inc. (pubdate 20171024), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: The purpose of these lidar data was to produce high accuracy 3D hydro-flattened digital elevation models (DEMs) with 0.5 and 1 meter cell sizes.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 LiDAR - Great Salt Lake AOIs, project-level FGDC metadata, Quantum Spatial, Inc. (pubdate 20171024), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: Elevation values were assigned to all Inland Ponds and Lakes, Inland Pond and Lake Islands, Inland Stream and River Islands, using TerraModeler functionality.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 LiDAR - Great Salt Lake AOIs, project-level FGDC metadata, Quantum Spatial, Inc. (pubdate 20171024), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: vertical datum of NAVD88 (GEOID12B), meters.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 LiDAR - Great Salt Lake AOIs, project-level FGDC metadata, Quantum Spatial, Inc. (pubdate 20171024), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: LiDAR data was acquired on September 3, 2016 through November 30, 2016 in 48 total lifts.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 - Great Salt Lake AOIs LiDAR Project Report, Quantum Spatial, Inc., submitted August 14, 2017 (Contract # AV2408), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: Great Salt Lake QL1 1,537 km2 Box Elder, Davis, Salt Lake, Tooele, and Weber Counties in northern Utah Great Salt Lake QL2 2,147 km2
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 - Great Salt Lake AOIs LiDAR Project Report, Quantum Spatial, Inc., submitted August 14, 2017 (Contract # AV2408), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: Hydro-flattened breaklines in Esri shapefile format • 0.5-meter hydro-flattened bare-earth raster DEM, tiled, in ERDAS .IMG format - QL1 • 1-meter hydro-flattened bare-earth raster DEM, tiled, in ERDAS .IMG format - QL2
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 - Great Salt Lake AOIs LiDAR Project Report, Quantum Spatial, Inc., submitted August 14, 2017 (Contract # AV2408), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: All geospatial deliverables were produced in NAD83 UTM Zone 12, meters; NAVD88 (GEOID12B), meters.

verbatim_quotes.quote: Elevation values were assigned to all Inland Ponds and Lakes, Inland Pond and Lake Islands, Inland Stream and River Islands, using TerraModeler functionality. Elevation values were assigned to all inland streams and rivers using Quantum Spatial, Inc. proprietary software.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 - Great Salt Lake AOIs LiDAR Project Report, Quantum Spatial, Inc., submitted August 14, 2017 (Contract # AV2408), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: Class 2 (Ground) lidar points in conjunction with the hydro breaklines were used to create hydro- flattened raster DEMs with a 0.5-meter cell size for the QL1 AOIs and a 1-meter cell size for the QL2 AOI.
verbatim_quotes.source: Utah 2016 - Great Salt Lake AOIs LiDAR Project Report, Quantum Spatial, Inc., submitted August 14, 2017 (Contract # AV2408), distributed by USGS

verbatim_quotes.quote: The seamless DEMs distributed by the USGS are hydroflattened, topographic raster DEMs that represent the bare ground (bare earth) surface excluding trees, buildings, and any other surface objects.
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9

verbatim_quotes.quote: Elevation values at each arc-second increment are derived through bilinear interpolation from source DEMs that are typically in Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) or State Plane coordinate space.
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9

verbatim_quotes.quote: Priority Data sources 1 High-resolution data derived from lidar, digital photogrammetry, or ifsar data. 2 10-meter DEMs derived from 1:24,000-scale cartographic contours and mapped hydrography. 3 2-arc-second (approximately 60-meter) DEMs derived from 1:63,360-scale cartographic contours.
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9

verbatim_quotes.quote: The seamless DEM product shall be a hydroflattened topographic DEM that is suitable for general mapping purposes and contour generation. Water surface elevations are established to support improved cartographic appearance only.
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9

verbatim_quotes.quote: The data source date for the seamless DEM product shall be the earliest month and year of the project data acquisition. The tile date shall be the month and year the project or tile was incorporated into the seamless DEM dataset.
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9

verbatim_quotes.quote: Under 3DEP, the legacy contour-generated DEM source is being systematically replaced with lidar-equivalent accuracy in CONUS
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9

verbatim_quotes.quote: Production Device: Windows version of LT4X by Titan Systems, Inc. Production Method: LT4X Production Site: Forest Service Data Source Date: 1948
verbatim_quotes.source: Archuleta et al. 2017, The National Map seamless digital elevation model specifications, USGS Techniques and Methods 11-B9, doi:10.3133/tm11B9
